codeReview.summary: The worker added .catch() handlers across many call sites and covered the named focus files, but the resulting implementation still leaves several fire-and-forget promises with empty catch callbacks, so silent failures remain and VAL-CRIT-005 is not fully satisfied.

issues.description: `this.injectContentScript(changedTabId).catch(() => {})` still swallows rejection silently during tab updates. This is still a floating promise without meaningful error handling, so recording content-script reinjection failures remain invisible.
`this.stopRecording().catch(() => {})` on tab removal still suppresses async stop failures. That recreates the same silent-failure behavior the feature was meant to remove.

`chrome.runtime.sendMessage({ type: 'recording_discard' }).catch(() => {})` still drops rejected runtime-message promises without logging or fallback handling, so discard failures remain unobservable.
`pruneOldTraces().catch(() => {})` still uses an empty catch callback, leaving trace-pruning failures silent instead of handled.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The cleanup-worker skill says floating promises should gain error handling, but it does not explicitly warn that replacing a floating promise with `.catch(() => {})` is still insufficient for this mission. The reviewed implementation used that pattern in multiple files.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: /Users/sero/projects/browser-ai/.factory/skills/cleanup-worker/SKILL.md says to add proper handling; commit 4f14eb76a788149bf43a9a881e094a4b21f22493 still leaves empty `.catch(() => {})` handlers in `packages/extension/recording/recording-coordinator.ts:233,240`, `packages/extension/sidepanel/ui/chat/panel-recorder.ts:229`, and `packages/extension/sidepanel/ui/core/state-manager.ts:41`.

summary: Fail: the feature improved many floating promises, but several remaining fire-and-forget paths still use empty `.catch(() => {})` callbacks, so silent async failures are still present.
